subject.title: Unhandled socket error in SSRF fetch wrapper can kill the gateway process (IPv6-only DNS + Happy Eyeballs)

question: Should the linked SSRF socket-error fix require live IPv6-unreachable proof and explicit preservation of pinned DNS/proxy behavior before this issue can close?
rationale: The remaining work changes a network security boundary and the current linked PR shows how an apparently narrow socket listener can weaken explicit-proxy pinning if applied at the wrong layer.

options.title: Require proof-preserving repair
options.body: Keep this issue open until the linked PR or replacement fix preserves pinned DNS/proxy behavior and shows the IPv6-only failure rejects without exiting the gateway.

options.title: Accept source-only proof
options.body: Allow a source-level/unit-tested fix to land without live IPv6-unreachable proof if maintainers decide the environment is too costly to reproduce.

options.title: Defer the crash fix
options.body: Leave the issue open as security-boundary debt while relying on operator mitigations such as IPv4-first DNS and restart policies.

recommendation.title: Require proof-preserving repair
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open until the linked PR or replacement fix preserves pinned DNS/proxy behavior and shows the IPv6-only failure rejects without exiting the gateway.

likelyOwner.reason: Current-line history points to recent work carrying the SSRF and fetch-guard paths forward, making this the best available routing candidate for the security-boundary choice.
